mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen monotonically for four consecutive weeks (-22.7 to -18.6), indicating a self-reinforcing recovery trend; this momentum should continue, pushing the next 4-week mean above the last 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact: RETAIL_REC increased each week from t-3w (-22.7) to t-0w (-18.6)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's weekly mean reverses and falls below -19.1 (the t-1w level) for two consecutive weeks, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility, currently oscillating near -30%, reflects residual transit-related restrictions; if TRANSIT crosses above -25% for two consecutive weeks, it signals relaxed transit curbs that feed through to increased retail visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -25 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT ranged -31.4 to -29.3 across the four weeks in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks of TRANSIT crossing -25, or TRANSIT crosses the threshold while RETAIL_REC's mean change remains flat or negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in WORKPLACES (from -24.4 to -15.7) alongside a stable TRANSIT level together indicate renewed in-person work attendance, which jointly drives higher weekday retail and recreation visits as commuters combine errands with their commute.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week while TRANSIT does not fall by more than 2 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES rebounded from -24.4 (t-1w) to -15.7 (t-0w) while TRANSIT stayed near -29 to -31
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the following two weeks despite joint WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improvement, or the co-movement shows no measurable correlation with RETAIL_REC growth.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility, hovering around 17-19% above baseline, reflects continued home-centric behavior; a decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility signals increased willingness to venture out, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the following month, but only while restrictions are actively easing.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 16 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL stayed between 17.4 and 19.6 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below the threshold but RETAIL_REC's mean does not increase over the next 28 days, or the relationship only holds during lockdown-tightening regimes rather than easing ones.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized in the low single digits (1.0 to 5.0), indicating that panic or precautionary grocery stocking has subsided; as this substitution behavior fades, consumer spending reallocates back toward retail and recreation outlets, lifting RETAIL_REC in the short term.
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM weekly means ranged from 1.0 to 5.0 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's weekly mean does not increase in the week following any decline of GROCERY_PHARM toward zero, falsifying the substitution-reversal mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility spiked to -7.6 at t-1w before falling back to -11.9, suggesting outdoor leisure can substitute for indoor retail activity; if PARKS visits rise sharply again, crossing above -8, consumers may favor outdoor recreation over retail trips, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth in the short term.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises above -8 week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS rose to -7.6 at t-1w before falling back to -11.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise even when PARKS crosses above -8, indicating no substitution effect between parks and retail mobility.

mechanism_narrative: As Singapore approaches the year-end holiday shopping season (December), historical seasonal patterns of increased retail and recreation activity are expected to compound the already-rising RETAIL_REC trend, producing a further increase over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: decision date falls within 6 weeks of the December holiday shopping period
evidence_refs: fact: decision point is 2021-11-15, six weeks before the year-end holiday period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to show above-baseline growth during the pre-holiday weeks, or the four-week mean does not exceed the prior four-week mean despite the approaching holiday season.

mechanism_narrative: The anomalous WORKPLACES dip at t-1w (-24.4) followed by a sharp rebound to -15.7 at t-0w indicates a transient disruption rather than a structural decline; continued mean reversion in WORKPLACES mobility should support increased weekday foot traffic, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly dip exceeds 8 points below the prior week followed by a rebound exceeding 5 points
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES fell to -24.4 at t-1w then rebounded to -15.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: The WORKPLACES rebound fails to translate into higher RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks, or WORKPLACES relapses below -20 again within that period.
